_comment: THE DEFECT LEDGER — the single source for every defect count this project states in prose (HOD-620). Counting rule: one entry per distinct defect with a distinct fix. A defect that recurs in a new place is a NEW entry, because the recurrence is the finding. A single defect with two compounding causes is ONE entry. Every entry names a primary source in this repository; nothing here is asserted without one. Counts are derived by scripts/count_defect_ledger.py into docs/metrics.json, and scripts/check_doc_metrics.py fails the build if any document's stated figure drifts from them. This file exists because the count was previously typed into seven documents by hand and had already drifted (fifteen in the blog, fourteen everywhere else).
counting_rule: one entry per distinct defect with a distinct fix; a recurrence in a new location is a new entry

classes.title: The boundary was live, and it was breakable

defects.summary: POST /api/v1/license took counterparty_id from the request body and used it as both the query filter and the session context the gateway checked the filter against, so the gateway compared the caller's claim to itself.
defects.source: docs/BUILD-LOG.md correction note #5; docs/FINDINGS.md named finding

defects.summary: POST /api/v1/revoke took no Request and called no authenticator, three lines below two handlers that do. Anonymous revocation of any published work_id, not undoable under an append-only log.
GET /internal/accrual_audit shipped public and appended a document on every call while its docstring claimed idempotence.

classes.title: My own infrastructure lied for me

defects.summary: SELF_UA_PATTERNS omitted python-requests and Hodi-Latency-Test, so the project's own boundary test and timing harness were counted as third-party crawler access.
The same list omitted Google-Cloud-Scheduler, so the project's own scheduled accrual job was counted as a third-party crawler, inverting the signature honesty finding into a fabricated positive.
defects.source: docs/BUILD-LOG.md correction note #7; docs/FINDINGS.md named finding

defects.summary: Third recurrence: Hodi-Adversarial-Audit/1.0, nine records from the developer's own IP, counted as non-self-originated. Fixed with a hodi- prefix RULE rather than a fourth enumeration entry.

classes.title: The guard passed perfectly and the property was false

defects.summary: resolve() folded events ordered by issued_at.isoformat() — the string, not the instant — so under mixed UTC offsets a revocation folded in ahead of the grant it revokes and permits() answered True for a revoked grant. The byte-stability check could not see it, because the fold was deterministically wrong rather than unstable.
test_grant_log_iam.py built a set literal and asserted membership in it — guarding the append-only invariant the entire audit trail rests on while touching no policy, no role and no datastore.
Prompt-injection detection had zero credential-free coverage; the only tests were gated behind a credentials flag, so emptying the detection patterns broke nothing.
The event_id sort tiebreak, documented as load-bearing for byte-stable replay, was never exercised because every fixture carried a distinct timestamp.

session_context appeared in zero test files, so neutering gateway.py::_enforce — the gateway copy of the cross-buyer rule that the deployed API and the public debug endpoint both depend on — left all 203 tests green.
Nothing asserted that the /api/v1/license handler folds the event log before testing containment; the mutation survived the suite.

The static honesty audit's pattern loop was dedented out of its file loop, so roughly four of five files in src/evidence were never scanned, and the assertion was an arbitrary floor rather than an exact set.
make demo used bare assert, so python3 -O printed 'ALL DEMO BEATS PASSED' beside contradictory output with the revocation invariant broken.

tests/test_buyer_api_e2e.py posted license bodies with no work_id and no counterparty_id, so both signed-request tests received HTTP 422 and asserted nothing about scope resolution or receipts. HODI_E2E-gated, skipped offline, and the workflow that runs them had never executed.
defects.source: docs/FINDINGS.md — a capability recorded as scripted, never run

defects.summary: test_discovery_does_not_disclose_deregistered_agents asserted len(found)==1 against AgentRegistry(), which defaults to the durable append-only store. It holds only against an empty registry, so it failed on a system behaving correctly. Rewritten to assert the actual property against a per-run agent id.
defects.source: docs/FINDINGS.md — a capability recorded as scripted, never run

defects.summary: The check used to conclude 'no traces are landing' was itself broken: the Cloud Trace v1 LIST endpoint returned 0 results for a window in which a span demonstrably existed — proven by writing one via v2 batchWrite and fetching it back by id, which found it. Every zero reading was an artifact of the query, producing confident evidence for a wrong conclusion.
defects.source: docs/FINDINGS.md — the durable trace backend could never have worked

defects.summary: tests/test_tracing_backend.py asserted that requesting cloud export yields a CONSOLE exporter, with a docstring stating 'the Cloud Trace exporter is not a pinned dependency'. That was true, and it was the bug: the test encoded the defect as the expected behaviour and stayed green for exactly as long as the durable backend was a no-op. Pinning the dependency turned it red in CI on the run that proved the backend works. Rewritten to force the ImportError so the fallback is tested as a property, plus the missing converse assertion that an installed AND authenticated exporter selects cloud.
defects.source: docs/FINDINGS.md — the durable trace backend could never have worked

defects.summary: Budget alerts, a cost-fenced project and a scheduler were all written up as complete in the build log. None existed. Reporting infrastructure as verified without an observed execution is itself the finding.

The live-verification workflow's KMS step required roles/cloudkms.signer on the CI identity — the power to forge any Hodi receipt — to sign a receipt and then verify the signature it had just made. A closed loop proving CI can use a key, not that the service is honest. It also set HODI_SIGNING=kms without HODI_KMS_KEY_VERSION, so it could never have run.
defects.source: docs/FINDINGS.md — a capability recorded as scripted, never run

defects.summary: With the exporter finally building, four real requests still produced zero traces: BatchSpanProcessor flushes on a background thread and Cloud Run throttles CPU to nothing between requests, so the flush was never scheduled. No error, no warning, no spans. Fixed with a bounded force_flush inside the request.
defects.source: docs/FINDINGS.md — the durable trace backend could never have worked

classes.title: Claims with no code behind them

defects.summary: ADK was named as the runtime agent framework in the README, the PRD and on Diagram A while google.adk appeared nowhere in the codebase; the only occurrence of the string was inside a print().

docs/VIDEO-SCRIPT.md carried a top banner warning that work_id had become mandatory on /api/v1/license and /api/v1/license/natural, while three of its four on-camera command bodies still omitted it. Executed against the deployed service on 2026-08-14, Beat 3 and the hero's Frames A and C each returned HTTP 422 'work_id Field required'. The warning was correct for days and changed nothing, because a banner is not a mechanism. Fixed and guarded by tests/test_recording_script_contract.py, which derives the route-to-model table from src/api/buyer_api.py rather than transcribing it.
defects.source: docs/FINDINGS.md — the recording script would have failed on camera

defects.summary: HODI_TRACE_EXPORT=cloud selected a Cloud Trace exporter whose package was not in requirements.lock, so the import failed and a bare `except: pass` fell back to the console. The durable trace backend could ONLY ever have been the console exporter, and the service reported healthy throughout.
defects.source: docs/FINDINGS.md — the durable trace backend could never have worked

classes.title: Policy looser than the policy text

defects.summary: get_action_permission() matched collections by PREFIX, so the permitted path template buyer_terms/{counterparty_id} also permitted an unfiltered read of the whole buyer_terms collection.

denied_collections sat in the policy data consulted by no enforcement code. No collection appeared in both lists, so deleting the deny-check produced identical output and the existing test still passed.
The gateway compared filter against session context only when the caller supplied one, so a call that omitted it was permitted — a check whose enforcement depended on the caller cooperating.

resolve() reported status 'superseded' while returning a live active_scope, active_grant_events() returned nothing, and permits() accepted the raw event and said yes. Three components, three answers, one event.
permits() validated per-iteration, so it returned a permissive answer before reaching an invalid event. The first version of the fix passed its own test while being wrong.

derived_scopes rendered list(set) under hash randomisation in the response body of POST /api/v1/revoke, while structured_derivation on the same object was sorted — one response carrying a stable and an unstable rendering of the same fact.
/evidence-counts hard-coded three zeros for canary_hit, verbatim_match and redistribution — literals on a live surface, against this project's own Literal Metric Rendering Rule.
The artist console was drawn writing to the Gateway and its code claimed it would POST to /api/v1/revoke. It cannot: revocation needs an artist credential a static SPA must not hold.

The hero beat's Frame A hardcoded valid_from: '2026-08-09T00:00:00Z' while make recording-prep seeds the demo grant with valid_from = now. permits() requires the request window to be contained in the grant window, so the request was correctly denied and the frame whose only job is to show the licence GRANTED returned permitted: false. Not a schema error — the request was well-formed and the answer was right — so no static check could have seen it as malformed; guarded instead by a specific assertion that request bodies do not hardcode valid_from.
defects.source: docs/FINDINGS.md — the recording script would have failed on camera

defects.summary: The recording script instructed the presenter to say on camera that the signature field reads UNSIGNED_PLACEHOLDER. Cloud KMS signing had shipped and the deployed service returns KMS-ECDSA-P256-SHA256:..., so the narration would have contradicted the screen and discarded the strongest provable claim in the submission. The inverse of this project's usual defect: the prose understated a mechanism that had become real.
defects.source: docs/FINDINGS.md — the recording script would have failed on camera

defects.summary: GET /works unioned the committed seed with persisted rows at ROW level, so every persisted row silently deleted the eight fields it did not carry: no canary on any work, no control_proof on the one verified_control work, and /works/{id}/proof answering HTTP 500. Overriding what a row asserts is correct; erasing what it is silent about is not.
defects.source: docs/FINDINGS.md — the public manifest was serving no canaries

defects.summary: The drill wrapped the delegation in its own root span and returned that trace id. The ADK runner roots its own `invocation` span in its own execution context, so the delegation is a different trace the wrapper does not adopt — measured as 12 spans, 11 under ADK's root and the wrapper alone in a second trace. The returned id resolved in Cloud Trace to a single useless span.
defects.source: docs/FINDINGS.md — the durable trace backend could never have worked

classes.title: Numbers stated in prose that no mechanism held to their source

defects.summary: README and Diagram B stated '160 accrued records, zero attributable to third parties' while the project's own documented make metrics regenerated a larger total and a non-zero third-party count.
The README claimed the overclaim lint caught training-membership phrasings 'including paraphrases'. Measured coverage against a 12-paraphrase probe set was 4.

The defect count itself: fifteen in the blog after the sort bug was added, fourteen in the README (twice), docs/index.md, the Devpost description, the Medium copy and social post 1. The count lived in seven documents and in no source, which is the same shape as the two defects above. This file and scripts/count_defect_ledger.py are the fix.

The README's deployed-path sentence stated 'revocation cascade 3049 ms cold / 534 ms warm average' while docs/metrics.json — named as its source one clause earlier — said 2263 / 736.6. The metrics file had been regenerated hours before after a real regression; the prose citing it had not. Every other published figure in the README was guarded by check_doc_metrics.py; latency figures were not, so that is where the drift went. Fixed by check_deployed_timings(), which also requires the sentence to name the revision the measurement came from.
defects.source: docs/FINDINGS.md — the recording script would have failed on camera

defects.summary: The deployment-status table in README.md is marked GENERATED and says not to hand-edit it. Nothing regenerated it and nothing compared it, so a promotion recorded in deployment_status.json would leave the README showing the old state and the old date. It was already stale by four rows.
defects.source: docs/FINDINGS.md — a capability recorded as scripted, never run
